Capital Master Plan In annex II to its report on the United Nations for the year ended 31 December 2019 (A/75/5 (Vol. I), chap. II), the Board provided a summary of the status of implementation of its 15 extant recommendations on the capital master plan relating to prior financial periods. Of those 15 recommendations, 13 (87 per cent) had been fully implemented and 2 (13 per cent) were under implementation. history.recommendation_text: In paragraph 576 of its report, the Board recommended that the Administration focus efforts on avoiding delays in project implementation, particularly for activities identified as being on the critical path, to avoid risk of cost escalation.
history.reference_raw: Report of the Board for the year ended 31 December 2018 6
history.sg_progress: Key activities on the critical path of the Africa Hall project include: design and documentation (including procurement); construction works; and handover and closeouts. The Economic Commission for Africa continues to focus on actions aimed at mitigating delays for the above activities and to avoid cost escalation. The following steps have been undertaken: (a) negotiation with the proposed contractor to reduce the time of implementation by 25 per cent; (b) monthly monitoring of the timeline at the project level; (c) quarterly revision of the timeline at the stakeholder level; (d) strict monitoring of supplier deadlines included in the weekly performance review; (e) backward planning for all tasks at the team level; and (f) weekly meetings with key players since 2020.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration focus efforts on avoiding delays in project implementation, particularly for activities identified as being on the critical path, to avoid risk of cost escalation.
history.administration_response: The Africa Hall project team has continued to focus effort on avoiding any delay in project implementation. The pending activity on the critical path is handover and commissioning. The following actions are being undertaken: (a) close monitoring of activities leading to the substantial completion. (Cost, project schedule in the critical path); (b) engagement with senior management and relevant stakeholders for timely decision-making; (c) close coordination and engagement with the final users and maintainers to whom the project will be handed to. The Economic Commission for Africa (ECA) requests that the implementation date be revised to align to the life of the project, as the actions to be undertaken are required throughout the project life.
history.board_assessment: Given that the efforts and key activities are still in progress, the Board considers this recommendation to be under implementation.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration focus efforts on avoiding delays in project implementation, particularly for activities identified as being on the critical path, to avoid risk of cost escalation.
history.administration_response: Africa Hall was successfully inaugurated on 21 October 2024. Notwithstanding the delay in the project’s implementation, thanks to the mitigations put in place by the Economic Commission for Africa (ECA), such as close schedule monitoring, meticulous change control and the adoption of a proactive approach to identified risks, the project was concluded without any cost escalation and within the original budget. Moreover, ECA has documented and shared lessons learned with the relevant stakeholders in order to inform the management of future construction projects. ECA requests the closure of this recommendation.
history.board_assessment: Given that the project was completed in February 2025 without any cost escalation and within the original budget, the Board considers the recommendation to be implemented.
